## All conformal maps from the unit disc $D(0,1)$ to the upper half-plane $\mathcal U$

**Notation.** $D=\{z\in\mathbb C:|z|<1\}$, $\mathcal U=\{w\in\mathbb C:\operatorname{Im}w>0\}$. "Conformal map" means a biholomorphic (one-to-one, onto, holomorphic with holomorphic inverse) map.

### Step 1. A reference map $\varphi:D\to\mathcal U$

Set
$$\varphi(z)=i\,\frac{1-z}{1+z}.$$
This is a Möbius transformation (hence biholomorphic on $\mathbb C\setminus\{-1\}$, in particular on $D$ since $-1\notin D$). For $z=x+iy$ with $|z|<1$,
$$\operatorname{Im}\varphi(z)=\operatorname{Re}\!\left(\frac{1-z}{1+z}\right)=\operatorname{Re}\!\left(\frac{(1-z)(1+\bar z)}{|1+z|^{2}}\right)=\frac{1-|z|^{2}}{|1+z|^{2}}>0.$$
So $\varphi(D)\subseteq\mathcal U$. When $|z|=1$ (boundary, $z\neq -1$), $\operatorname{Im}\varphi(z)=0$, so the unit circle maps onto the real axis; and $\varphi(0)=i\in\mathcal U$, $\varphi(1)=0$, $\varphi(-1)=\infty$. Being a non-constant Möbius map sending the boundary circle to the boundary line, $\varphi$ maps $D$ **onto** $\mathcal U$. Thus $\varphi$ is a conformal map $D\to\mathcal U$.

### Step 2. Automorphisms of the disc

A standard consequence of the Schwarz lemma: every conformal automorphism of $D$ has the form
$$M(z)=e^{i\theta}\frac{z-a}{1-\bar a\,z},\qquad a\in D,\ \theta\in\mathbb R.$$
These are exactly the biholomorphic self-maps of $D$; denote this group $\operatorname{Aut}(D)$.

### Step 3. Reduction of the general map

Let $f:D\to\mathcal U$ be any conformal (biholomorphic) map. Then
$$\varphi^{-1}\circ f:D\longrightarrow D$$
is a biholomorphic self-map of $D$, i.e. an element of $\operatorname{Aut}(D)$. Writing $M=\varphi^{-1}\circ f\in\operatorname{Aut}(D)$, we obtain
$$f=\varphi\circ M.$$
Conversely, every map of the form $\varphi\circ M$ with $M\in\operatorname{Aut}(D)$ is a composition of biholomorphisms, hence a conformal map $D\to\mathcal U$.

Therefore **the set of all conformal maps $D\to\mathcal U$ is exactly**
$$\boxed{\;f(z)=\varphi(M(z))=i\,\frac{1-e^{i\theta}\frac{z-a}{1-\bar a z}}{1+e^{i\theta}\frac{z-a}{1-\bar a z}},\qquad a\in D,\ \theta\in\mathbb R.\;}$$

### Step 4. Explicit Möbius form

Clearing the inner denominator,
$$f(z)=i\,\frac{(1-\bar a z)-e^{i\theta}(z-a)}{(1-\bar a z)+e^{i\theta}(z-a)}
=i\,\frac{(1+e^{i\theta}a)-(\bar a+e^{i\theta})\,z}{(1-e^{i\theta}a)-(\bar a-e^{i\theta})\,z}.$$

This is a Möbius transformation $\frac{\alpha z+\beta}{\gamma z+\delta}$. Writing $A=\bar a+e^{i\theta}$ and using the conjugate-pair structure, one may equivalently parametrize the whole family as
$$f(z)=\frac{A+\overline{A}\,z}{B+\overline{B}\,z},\qquad A,B\in\mathbb C,\quad \operatorname{Im}(A\overline{B})>0,$$
defined up to a common real scalar multiple of $(A,B)$ (the inequality guarantees the image is the upper half-plane, not the lower one; the conjugate-pair form guarantees the unit circle is sent to the real axis).

### Step 5. Equivalence with the $\operatorname{Aut}(\mathcal U)$ parametrization

The automorphism group of $\mathcal U$ is $\operatorname{PSL}(2,\mathbb R)$:
$$T(w)=\frac{\alpha w+\beta}{\gamma w+\delta},\qquad \alpha,\beta,\gamma,\delta\in\mathbb R,\ \alpha\delta-\beta\gamma>0.$$
Since $\varphi\circ M\circ\varphi^{-1}\in\operatorname{Aut}(\mathcal U)$, every $\varphi\circ M$ can be rewritten as $T\circ\varphi$ for some $T\in\operatorname{PSL}(2,\mathbb R)$, and vice versa. Hence an equivalent description is
$$f(z)=\frac{\alpha\,\varphi(z)+\beta}{\gamma\,\varphi(z)+\delta}
=\frac{\alpha\, i(1-z)+\beta(1+z)}{\gamma\, i(1-z)+\delta(1+z)},\qquad \begin{pmatrix}\alpha&\beta\\ \gamma&\delta\end{pmatrix}\in\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb R).$$

Both parametrizations are 3-real-parameter families (parameters $a\in D$ — 2 real — and $\theta\in\mathbb R$, or equivalently $\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb R)$ modulo sign — 3 real dimensions), as expected since each of $D$ and $\mathcal U$ has a 3-dimensional automorphism group and the space of conformal maps between them is a torsor for either.

### Conclusion

Every conformal map of the unit disc $D(0,1)$ onto the upper half-plane $\mathcal U$ is a Möbius transformation, and the totality of them is
$$f(z)=i\,\frac{1-e^{i\theta}\frac{z-a}{1-\bar a z}}{1+e^{i\theta}\frac{z-a}{1-\bar a z}},\qquad |a|<1,\ \theta\in\mathbb R,$$
equivalently $f=T\circ\varphi$ with $\varphi(z)=i(1-z)/(1+z)$ and $T\in\mathrm{PSL}(2,\mathbb R)$.
